costOfLiving.heading: What is cost of living?
subPara: The cost of living refers to the total amount of money required to maintain a basic standard of living in a specific location. It includes essential expenses like housing, food, transportation, healthcare, education, utilities, and discretionary spending such as entertainment.

It varies significantly due to factors like location (metro vs. non-metro), lifestyle choices, family size, and inflation. While urban areas like Mumbai, Delhi, and Bangalore have a high cost of living, smaller towns and villages offer a more affordable lifestyle.

items.title: Housing (Rent & EMI)​
items.desc:
Housing costs take up a major chunk of your budget. In metro cities, a 1BHK can cost ₹15,000 - ₹50,000, while smaller cities offer lower rents at ₹8,000 - ₹20,000.
Home loan EMIs range from ₹30,000 - ₹80,000, making financial planning essential. Use our Home Loan EMI Calculator to estimate and manage your payments.

items.title: Food & Groceries​
items.desc:
Food expenses can quickly add up. A family of four spends ₹5,000 - ₹15,000 monthly on groceries, and inflation makes essentials pricier.
Frequent dining out further increases costs. Track your food budget with our Budget Planner and make informed spending choices.

items.title: Transportation (Fuel & Commuting)​
items.desc: Transportation is another key expense. Public transport costs around ₹1,500/month, but car owners face fuel prices of ₹90-₹110 per litre, plus maintenance, tolls, and parking.

items.title: Healthcare & Medical Expenses
items.desc: Healthcare expenses can be unpredictable. A doctor’s visit costs ₹500 - ₹1,500, while health insurance with ₹5L coverage costs ₹8,000 - ₹12,000 annually. Hospitalization can reach ₹2L - ₹5L.​

items.title: Education & Childcare
items.desc:
Education is a major investment. Private school fees range from ₹50,000 - ₹2L per year, and higher education can cost ₹10L - ₹25L. Coaching and tuition add to the burden.
Start building a secure financial future with smart savings—explore our Investment Plans to grow your funds steadily.

items.title: Utilities & Discretionary Spending
items.desc: Utilities and lifestyle expenses—electricity, internet, shopping, and entertainment—add ₹3,000 - ₹8,000 to monthly budgets. Managing these wisely ensures financial stability.
